source:
# Port of lib/pubid/iho/parser.rb — IHO identifiers: letter series
# (S/P/M/B/C), a number with an optional suffix, and the full component
# tail (edition, supplement, part, annex, appendix + subnumber, volume,
# issue, year qualifier).
#
# == Component model (owner rulings, 2026-11-03)
#
# Every component below is a first-class semantic component: its own
# named capture, its own typed binding, independently addressable in
# the model, URN-encodable and matchable — never a regex/string suffix.
#
#   component    face                capture             binding type
#   edition      x.y.z (bare)        edition             string
#   edition      v1 / v5.1 (alias)   edition_shorthand   string (parse-only;
#                                                        the builder pads to
#                                                        x.y.0 — official IHO
#                                                        edition is dotted
#                                                        x.y.z WITHOUT a year)
#   volume       Vol. N              volume              string
#   volume       /N (short)          volume              string (the slash
#                                                        chain, P-1/21 or
#                                                        P-5/2020)
#   volume       N (bare, legacy)    volume              string (the yearbook
#                                                        year IS a volume —
#                                                        one serial-locator
#                                                        component)
#   issue        (N) / Issue N       issue               string
#   year         (2024)              year                string (the with-year
#                                                        qualifier on
#                                                        standards; NOT a
#                                                        serial locator)
#
# The part has a COMPACT face, hyphenated onto the code - `IHO S-5-B`
# (lettered part) and `IHO S-100-1` (numbered part) - which both parses
# and renders; the canonical expanded face stays `IHO S-100 x.y.z
# Part 1`. Gluing a part onto the code without a separator (S-5A) is
# DISALLOWED as a form: it cannot extend to numbered parts without
# ambiguity (S-1001 = series 1001 vs series 100 part 1). The four
# lettered bases the corpus records (S-5A, S-5B, S-8A, S-8B) are
# LEGACY data spellings: they still parse as aliases (S-5A == S-5
# Part A) but are never rendered; the owner rules later whether to
# reject them outright.
#
# Two main syntaxes per the owner ruling: `IHO S-100 1.0.0` (dated =
# edition-specific) and `IHO S-100` (undated = edition-non-specific).
# A year beside an edition is the with-year variant qualifier
# (`IHO S-100 1.0.0 Part X (2024)`), never a year-keyed docidentifier —
# year-keyed docidentifiers for edition-keyed products are wrong. The
# continuously-updated series have ONE serial locator, the volume:
# P-1 and P-6 are volume-keyed (`IHO P-1 Vol. 30 (1)`), and the
# yearbook year IS a volume (`IHO P-5 Vol. 2020`) — the bare year
# (`IHO P-5 2020`) and all year-faced forms are parse-only legacy
# aliases that bind into the volume component, never rendered.
#
# Aliases: "Suppl" (canonical face Sup, the M-2 spelling — why abbreviate
# by two letters when Annex and Appendix stay full-length), "App"/"Ap."
# (canonical face Appendix), the hyphenated compact part face (S-5-B ==
# S-5 Part B, S-100-1 == S-100 Part 1), the legacy glued lettered bases
# (S-5A, parse-only), "S-100 v1..v5.1" (edition shorthand), "Issue N"
# (canonical (N)), the bare year (canonical Vol. N).
#
# == URN segment grammar (positional, containment-ordered)
#
# The URN mirrors the containment tree, one semantic atom per segment:
# Part contains Annexes; Annex contains Appendices; a D-2 subnumber is
# a child atom of Appendix D. No key.value concatenations — every
# non-number component is a marker-prefixed segment whose marker is the
# lowercased human-face token (edition follows ISO's ed- precedent):
#
#   urn:iho:<type>:<number>[:ed-<x.y.z>][:sup-<n>][:part-<X>]
#     [:annex-<A>][:appendix-<B>][:<sub>][:vol-<n>][:issue-<n>]
#     [:year-<yyyy>]
#
#   position  segment          value vocabulary            containment
#   --------  ---------------  --------------------------  ------------------
#   1         <type>           s / p / m / b / c           namespace root
#   2         <number>         digits + : suffix; may      document code
#                              span bare segments until
#                              the first marker
#   3         ed-<x.y.z>       dotted a.b.c                edition qualifier
#   4         sup-<n>          1*digit                     wraps the base
#   5         part-<X>         letter (case kept) or       contains annexes
#                              digits [*letter]
#   6         annex-<A>        upper letter (case kept)    contains appendices
#   7         appendix-<B>     upper letter or digits      contains subnumber
#   8         <sub>            1*digit, BARE, only         child of appendix
#                              directly after appendix-
#   9         vol-<n>          1*digit (incl. yearbook     contains issue
#                              years, Vol. 2020)
#   10        issue-<n>        1*digit, only after vol-    child of volume
#   11        year-<yyyy>      19xx/20xx                   the standards
#                                                          with-year qualifier;
#                                                          periodicals have no
#                                                          year segment (their
#                                                          year is the volume)
#
# The number occupies every leading bare segment up to the first
# marker, so a colon number (S-158:100) round-trips without escaping;
# after the markers the only bare segment allowed is the appendix
# subnumber in its own slot. Both the year qualifier and the volume are
# marker-tagged so neither can collide with a colon-number segment (the
# #637 hazard, kept under the positional scheme). Letters are
# case-preserved: part-A and part-a are distinct documents.
#
# Legacy 2.0.x spellings remain decodable but are never emitted: the
# bare a.b.c segment (edition), the dotted keys part./annex./suppl./
# ap./appendix./vol./issue. and the single-letter y. year tag (whose
# value decodes into the volume — the serial-locator unification).
#
# Edition 2: ruby#400's capture-flatten keeps text captures over
# reference-built rules as the matched text, so the v2 tree is the v1
# tree plus named leaves for non-captured structure.

grammar PubidIho version "0.2.0" edition 2 {
  digit = %x30-39
  upper = %x41-5A
  lower = %x61-7A
  letter = upper / lower
  space = " "
  dash = "-"
  dot = "."

  series = ("S" / "P" / "M" / "B" / "C") as type
  number_suffix = (":" 1*digit)
  number = (1*digit [number_suffix]) as number
  # The compact part face, hyphenated onto the code: S-5-B (lettered)
  # and S-100-1 (numbered) — the dash replaces the old bare-glued
  # suffix, so a number like S-1001 stays a whole number (the dash is
  # what makes the part unambiguous). The dash-digit suffix that used
  # to join the number (P-6-3 as number "6-3") is now the part
  # component. The dash is an inlined literal: a named dash ref here
  # collides with the sequence's own dash node in the edition-2 tree.
  compact_part = "-" ((1*digit [*letter]) / upper) as part
  # LEGACY glued lettered bases (S-5A, S-5B, S-8A, S-8B in the corpus):
  # parse-only aliases, never rendered. Kept because the records exist;
  # the owner rules later whether to reject them.
  glued = upper as part

  # The official edition is the dotted x.y.z; "v1"/"v5.1" is the S-100
  # shorthand (parse-only, the builder pads to x.y.0).
  edition = space (1*digit dot 1*digit dot 1*digit) as edition
  v_edition = space "v" ((1*digit) ["." (1*digit)]) as edition_shorthand
  # The with-year qualifier on standards: a parenthesized year beside an
  # edition. This is the ONLY year capture — periodical years are
  # volumes (the serial-locator unification).
  year_qualifier = space "(" (("19" / "20") 2*digit) as year ")"

  supplement = space ("Suppl" / "Sup") space (1*digit) as supplement
  part = space "Part" space ((1*digit *letter) / upper) as part
  annex = space "Annex" space upper as annex
  appendix_value = (upper / (1*digit)) as appendix
  appendix_subnumber = dash (1*digit) as appendix_subnumber
  appendix = space ("Appendix" / "App" / "Ap.") space appendix_value [appendix_subnumber]

  volume = space "Vol." space (1*digit) as volume [volume_issue]
  volume_issue = (space "Issue" space (1*digit) as issue) / (space "(" (1*digit) as issue ")")
  # The volume's short face — the slash chain ("IHO P-1/21",
  # "IHO P-5/2020"). The slash no longer joins the number.
  volume_short = "/" ((1*digit) as volume)
  # LEGACY bare year ("IHO P-5 2024"): the yearbook year IS a volume,
  # so a bare year binds INTO the volume component. Parse-only alias;
  # the canonical print is "Vol. N".
  volume_year = space (("19" / "20") 2*digit) as volume

  # The edition slot accepts the dotted form or the v-shorthand; the
  # with-year qualifier may sit right after it. A second dated slot at
  # the end keeps the historical edition-last spellings parseable.
  dated = {
    (edition / v_edition)
    [year_qualifier]
  }

  # The serial tail picks exactly one discriminator: the long volume
  # (with its optional issue) or the legacy bare year — both bind the
  # volume component.
  serial = {
    (volume / volume_year)
  }

  identifier = {
    [("IHO" space)]
    series
    dash
    number
    [compact_part]
    [glued]
    [volume_short]
    [dated]
    [supplement]
    [part]
    [annex]
    [appendix]
    [serial]
    [year_qualifier]
    [dated]
  }

  entry identifier: identifier

  test {
    accept "S-5"
    accept "IHO S-5 Appendix 2"
    accept "IHO B-12 3.0.0"
    accept "IHO P-5 2024"
    accept "P-5 2024"
    accept "IHO P-5 Vol. 2024"
    accept "IHO P-5/2024"
    accept "IHO B-7 Vol. 2023"
    accept "IHO P-1 Vol. 30"
    accept "IHO P-1 Vol. 30 (2)"
    accept "IHO P-1 Vol. 30 Issue 2"
    accept "IHO P-1/21"
    accept "IHO P-1/21 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-100 5.0.0 Part 2"
    accept "IHO S-98 1.0.0 Part A"
    accept "IHO S-65 1.1.0 Annex A"
    accept "IHO S-122 1.0.0 Appendix D-2"
    accept "IHO S-52 4.0.0 Appendix 1"
    accept "IHO M-2 Sup 1"
    accept "IHO M-2 Suppl 6"
    accept "IHO S-66 2.0.0 Sup 4"
    accept "IHO S-5-B"
    accept "IHO S-100-1"
    accept "IHO S-100-1 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO P-6-3 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-5A"
    accept "IHO S-5A 1.0.2"
    accept "IHO S-5 1.0.2 Part A"
    accept "IHO S-100 5.0.0 Part 2 (2024)"
    accept "IHO S-100 v5.1"
    accept "IHO S-100 v1"
    accept "IHO S-100 1.0.0 (2024) Part A"
    accept "IHO S-53 Ap. 1 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-98 Part A 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-158:100 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-158:100 Part 2 1.0.0"
    accept "IHO S-1001"
    reject "nonsense"
    reject "IHO B-12 3.0"
    reject "IHO P-5 1850"
  }

  bindings identifier {
    type -> type (string)
    number -> number (string)
    part -> part (string)
    annex -> annex (string)
    appendix -> appendix (string)
    appendix_subnumber -> appendix_subnumber (string)
    supplement -> supplement (string)
    edition -> edition (string)
    edition_shorthand -> edition_shorthand (string)
    year -> year (string)
    volume -> volume (string)
    issue -> issue (string)
  }
}
